author: RUTHINAS
content:
Yes. I started at level 34, but it probably would have worked even earlier. Importantly it was well before any of the tanking tools added by Turtle. Outdamaging your party is your aggro, so it's quite dependent on gear. Leveling as Slow & Steady tends to help, since your levels don't keep up with your gear progression. I would consider engineering as pretty much a necessity; grenades give you a lot of area threat and survivability, target dummies can be used to taunt mobs off squishy party members, and spell reflectors help a ton with key caster mobs.

Some level 60 dungeons will be extremely tricky due to recent changes making specific elemental mobs immune to poisons, Dire Maul: West being one of the more frustrating examples. Also, lacking a taunt there are several raid bosses that can not be feasibly tanked by rogues (but on the other hand some, where the taunt mechanic is not a necessary consideration if the boss is tanked by a rogue, so look out for those). However, despite these difficulties and certain nerfs, rogues maintain a certain viability even into raid content. It is however rather difficult to get most guilds to diverge from the warrior tank status quo, even if for some encounters rogues are clearly the better choice.

As a final tip I recommend you unlearn the need to build large combos. As a tank your task is to maintain threat on multiple targets, meaning that sticking to building combos will prevent target swaps to a detrimental degree. I recommend building one or two combo points, casting slice and dice (if it needs refreshing) and moving to the next target. 5-combo eviscerates are not something you will be doing outside of single target boss encounters.

author: RUTHINAS
content:
**Leveling talents**
[Updated September 16th 2025]
The reworked talent trees are all suited for leveling up, although builds based around Backstab, and builds centered around the Subtlety tree, are more suited for group leveling. There is a technique called 'frontstabbing' that allows for the use of Backstab even in solo content, but it can be a bit unwieldy.

I'd argue that there is no "ideal" leveling build, as it all comes down to preference. However, some individual talents are more valuable for leveling up than others.

Improved Gouge is a literal lifesaver in a multitude of situations, but its greatest value comes from allowing one to bandage during combat (against a single target, or against two if you're able to use Blind or Kidney Shot on the other, or even three if you use all of the aforementioned abilities, though you will need to pay attention to your energy pool).

Lightning Reflexes and Deflection both improve your survivability by a fair amount, and they synergise well with Riposte and Setup, converting avoidance into damage output. They're less beneficial if you are leveling up with a tank, but don't be afraid to tank yourself; rogues _can_ tank all instances in the game if one so desires.

Improved Dual Wield is one of the greatest damage increasing talents, and Precision both improves your damage output and makes hitting important abilities more reliable (imagine missing that lifesaving Gouge!), so getting them is of key importance if heading down the Combat tree.

Ruthlessness has been changed to provide a 100% chance of retaining a combo point after using a finisher, which can also be used to "drift" a combo point to another target: certain finishers can be used even if you are not currently targeting the enemy which your combo is built on, and by doing so the extra combo point is transferred to your new target.

Improved Blade Tactics is fantastic as well, and so is Relentless Strikes.

Improved Ambush can be used to deal immense opener damage.

author: RUTHINAS
content:
The basic idea of rogue gameplay is maintaining Slice and Dice constantly. It is your most powerful ability. After your opener it would be ideal to cast it as soon as you are able to (usually at one or two combo points) and refreshing it when it is about to run out. While the buff will last longer per combo point, gaining those combo points costs energy. Using the finisher at low combo points will be more economical in terms of energy expenditure, but will give you a shorter window to do other things. Find a balance that fits the situation best.

You may sometimes get a chance to use other finishers too; if the target will stay alive long enough for the damage over time effect to run its course, Rupture is a solid alternative to Eviscerate, but if the enemy is close to death you will want to hit Eviscerate instead. If you need to, you can Kidney Shot a mob to reduce the pressure on the tank(s) and healer(s), but be aware that many raid mobs will be immune to it. You can and should use Flourish to increase your parry chance when mobs turn to attack you, or if you are fighting mobs with multi-target melee abilities like Whirlwind or area knockbacks. Any damage you don't take is mana a healer does not need to spend!

author: RUTHINAS
content:
This would probably serve you quite well as a Combat-centered dagger leveling build:

Start with **Improved Gouge**, then go for **2/5 Lightning Reflexes** to reach the second row of talents. Pick up **Precision** first, then **Blade Flurry**, only then backtrack to get **Improved Backstab**.

At this point, you can optionally pick up **Remorseless Attacks** from the Assassination tree if you tend to play solo, but for dungeon leveling you can skip it and move directly over to Subtlety for **Opportunity** and **Improved Ambush**.

After this, select a talent point of your choice in the Combat tree (my preference is **1/5 Deflection** for extra avoidance, as parry is slightly stronger than dodge due to "parry haste" which makes your next attack connect faster after parrying) to unlock the next row and take **Dual Wield Specialization**, then **Blade Rush** and **Close Quarters Combat**.

Then, dedicate your final points into the Assassination tree. Take **Malice**, follow up with **Ruthlessness** and **Improved Blade Tactics** to more easily maintain your Slice and Dice buff, and finish off with **Relentless Strikes** and **Lethality**.

If you did not pick up Remorseless Attacks, the final two points are free-form in placement. I feel like **Improved Sprint** has saved my skin quite often. To get the most out of it, you can pick it up earlier rather than later.

Alternative talent strategies exist too, so feel free to experiment. Serrated Blades is a great talent in the Subtlety tree, Surprise Attack grants some really solid combo generation, and is followed by Weapon Expertise for a strong source of dagger skill, to name a few examples.

Ultimately you will want to respec out of this leveling build at 60, but this should get you there with relative ease. Since Ambush is heavily emphasized, you will not have to "frontstab" as much (which is admittedly not a playstyle for everyone – certainly not for me at the very least).

Enjoy, and good luck!

author: RUTHINAS
content:
Like said above, you get a threat-generating poison. That is at 60, however, so leveling up your threat is generated solely by your damage. This means you will want to level up with the build that deals the most of it.

My personal recommendation is a Combat-centered build. Riposte helps a lot with both threat and survivability, Blade Flurry gives you solid threat on multiple targets (though you might nonetheless want to pick up engineering for things like grenades and target dummies), Setup grants you combo points and overall the Combat talents provide a lot of value for a tank.

You will want to unlearn some fundamentals of rogue gameplay to perform better as a tank. For instance combo points can be a trap; focus too much on one target and the others will harass your party. Therefore I recommend using small combos to refresh your key damage (and threat) buff, Slice and Dice, and swapping targets often to build up threat on all of them, losing some combo points in the process. This is quite fine especially leveling up, as hardly any of your damage comes from abilities such as Eviscerate. Later on at level 42 you will get a 20% party finisher, Flourish, that you'd ideally use more combo points for. You could, for example, open on a pack of mobs with Blade Flurry and Ghostly Strike, then a couple of Sinister Strikes along with Setup pointss, and finish the combo with Flourish as Ghostly Strike is about to wear off. The extra parry then very reliably procs Riposte, which does not generate combo points, allowing you to cast it on a secondary target before returning to the one where your combo points are built on.

Grenades provide an additional solution to multi-target threat and their incapacitate effect also buys healers a bit of extra time. Target dummies provide you with a "taunt" button of sorts, allowing you to more easily clump together a pack of mobs, or peel from your allies.

At 60 you'll want to look into an Envenom build, as it grants a lot of threat.

author: RUTHINAS
content:
A quite typical Combat/Assassination leveling build works very well. Damage is threat, so pick up what you need to maintain aggro, while getting avoidance talents, Riposte, Blade Flurry (very good for multi-target threat, but I recommend engineering grenades additionally).

Setup gives you a fair bit of combo points for all sorts of valuable utility, but losing your combo to generate threat on other targets is typical; while most of your threat comes from auto-attacks in one way or another, abilities can provide good burst threat when someone else is stealing aggro.

Adrenaline Rush is a great threat cooldown, but the extra energy can be converted into avoidance and utility abilities too. After getting it I would shift my focus to Assassination for Ruthlessness (which is honestly good enough to warrant picking up earlier too, maybe after Blade Flurry?), Improved Blade Tactics and and Relentless Strikes.

At 60 you can supplement your build with Improved Poisons for better Agitating Poison threat, or you can change to a dedicated poisoner build with Envenom for fantastic threat and a fairly interesting gameplay of using lots of low-combo finishers, keeping track of specific timings.

author: Repose
content:
Blade Flurry: Now baseline at level 30, no longer has a duration, cooldown reduced from 2 minutes to 4 seconds, and instead works as a toggled effect. Blade Flurry reduces energy generation by 30% and reduces damage dealt by 20% while active.

Developer Comment: Blade Flurry is moving from a long cooldown ability to a toggled effect, reducing damage and energy regeneration but granting a cleave effect.

While juggling the cooldown of your only cleave effect is a skill of its own, in practice it didn't give Rogues this agency as it was often used right off cooldown whenever multiple enemies are being fought.

This change will move the decision making away from spending a high cooldown or not and instead allows Rogues more agency in keeping it active or not, losing possible Energy if not properly timed.

oh install supercleveroidmacros (together with superwow, nampower and unitxp3), and have a nice easier syntax for macros:
/cast [combo:<#3] !Envenom
/cast [combo:<#3] !Slice and Dice
/cast [combo:#5, @target, type:"Elite"] !Rupture
/cast [combo:#5] Eviscerate

author: Rheinwg
content:
This is how it works:
For abilities:
- You need 5% hit to never miss an enemy of the same lvl
- You need 8% hit to never miss an enemy 3 lvls above you (that would be 1% hit per enemy lvl)
- Every point of weapon skill provides you with 0.2% hit, which is not shown as part of the "hit" stat on your character sheet
- Dodge and parry chance on the enemy are not affected by hit

For autoattacks:
- When you equip 2 weapons you get a hit penalty, this means your _autoattacks_ can be missed.
- This miss chance is FOR BOTH weapons, your mainhand autoattacks can miss too
- To completely offset that penalty you need to reach 25% hit (counting weapon skill)
- This means hit will provide a benefit to you up to 25%
- Hit also raises the crit cap for autoattacks

author: Rheinwg
content:
As far as abilities go:
- You should have at least 2 Shadow of Deaths and 2 Marks on every single fight. Unless you are fighting 2 bosses in a row with very little downtime like Gluth and Thaddius, because Prep has a 7min cd
- You want to see Hemo and Ghostly strike only, not backstab or sinister strikes

Uptimes are kind of difficult, because it depends on whether you are using IEA or not; juggling different finishers takes a significant toll on energy, and could be a big problem if you dont have extra energy coming from totems/bonuses.
- If you are using IEA you should see a high uptime. In the best case scenario: IEA is used on the 4 GCD, and every 30 seconds for the entire duration of the fight
- TotT should be up like 90% of the time, but is possible to reach more than that.
- Both SnD and Taste for blood should have a high uptime (SnD can even reach 100%), but they only benefit the rogue. And maintaining a perfect uptime on both is kinda hard if you are taking care of IEA, and much easier if you arent.

Also, all of this depends on the fight, keeping IEA/TFB/SND/TotT is really easy on Anomalus, but you will never have a 100% uptime of them on Gnarlmoon or Mephistroth. Also IEA is useless on KT or Skeram

Blackjack also exists, if you need that 10% damage reduction on the boss you should talk to your rogue on what is the best way to use it.

content:
Rotation: Try open with Garrote if you can, 1 more cp at start results faster first iEA. Then spam hemo till first 5cp to iEA, then I like to do a 1cp SnD to follow up, then Hemo till 3 cp, Mark, then use Shadow of Death.
After just try keep up SnD and uses Shadow of Death on cd while prio keeping up 5cp iEA.
Gearwise just what you got, but highly recommend to get The Ripper from SWV, it is the bis offhand for iEA. DO NOT USE Annihilator if we have Shart'ateth Axe in raid!! They use the same debuff slot and dont stack, they will keep overriding each other, bis weapon will be MH Anni and OH The Ripper. 
Poison for iEA rogue is almost the same as combat rogues, just need to remember on Medivh and Sanv you need to use double mind numbing poison. 
Prep is only 7min CD so you can pop it for extra Mark and Shadow of Death on each boss at excute phase.

author: Vegybird
content:
One hint on using this spec, you dont need to worry to much if you cant maintain SnD up 100%, dont wait and time it till the last sec, it is better to watch your Tricks of the Trade buff, it only lasts 12 sec, so ideally you want to cast a 5cp finisher every 11 sec, so you can maintain 2 stacks of this buff for your party, it is more important than SnD uptime or Shadow of death on CD.
But still iEA 5cp up 100% is the first goal
so if iEA has less than 10s or close to 10s, I wouldn't use another finisher, will refresh it first then use others later.
If you can speak on disc during raid, it is the best you call out before you about to do Mark, so your can get your party to use their bursts together for the extra dmg, 30% more ap for 8 sec is crazy.
Some extra advance play if you want to be pro:
Open with Sap then Garrote, sap will be immuned but it applies a 10% dmg reduction on boss for 8 sec. Unless warrior tank complain not getting hit hard enough to get rage, this is some extra dmg reduction, also Blind does the same effect too and it can also be prep. If you also have energy to spare, use distract on cd it also gives a good -6% hit on boss(guaranteed apply) for 6 sec.
Smoke bomb - I haven't found a good use in our raid in k40 yet, if you found one please share.....
Now class dismissed, you are the favorite rogue in the raid.

author: Rheinwg
content:
What poisons should i use on each raid?

Before we start: 

- Every spec with envenom should be using dissolvent/instant (Edit: Apparently Deadly and Cor are actually pretty good for Combat envenom) 
- Meanwhile Combat and Sub should change from instant poisons to dot poisons depending on the length of the fight, usually if the fight is over 40s long is better to use dot poisons, if is shorter you have to use instant/dissolvent.

Molten Core: 

- Trash:  The entirety of Molten Core is filled with different kind of enemies, but the most usual ones are Elementals and Giants. For this reason is recommended to use Dissolvent poison 2 for most of the trash, just put the Core Hounds on low priority. The only exception is the section with a green line where you should use Instant poison

- Bosses: Garr, Geddon, the Two Golems and the Undead Dwarf can only be damaged by Dissolvent or Corrosive.  The Salamander, the Core Hound, Sulfuron, Shazzrah and Mayordmo can only be damaged with Instant and Deadly. Golemagg is a giant and can be damage by both kind of poisons.

On the image: Orange is dissolvent and corrosive, green is instant and deadly

author: Rheinwg
content:
Black Wing Lair:

All of the enemies can be damage only with instant and deadly, with 3 exceptions:

- Spellbinders are inmune to all poisons, put them on low prio
- Drakonoids: These guys can have a high nature vulnerability, watch out for those to increase your damage
- Chromaggus: Chromaggus switches between high resitance and vulnerability to nature, meaning that your damage will vary, but only instant and deadly can damage him anyways

So, again, Assa: instant all the way. Combat: Instant for trash, the 2 max rank of Deadly for Bosses.

author: Rheinwg
content:
Temple of Ahn'Qiraj

All of the enemies can be damage only with instant and deadly, with 1 exception:

- Twins, are inmune to all poisons (fuck us apparently)

And you should be using Frost Oils for Viscidus

author: Rheinwg
content:
Naxxramas:

- Trash: Since most of the raid is composed of undead you are safe to use both kind of poisons. But there are several humanoids and beast around the instance, making instant the easier pick to be able to damage everyone.

- Bosses: most of bosses can be hurt with both kind of poisons, with the exception of Faerlina, Maexxna, and Gothik. Assa can run with either diss or instant, meanwhile combat and sub should be using Deadly 5 and Corrosive 2 on most bosses, and using Deadly 5 + Deadly 4 on Faerlina and Maexxa. Gothik is only dissolvent.

On the image: green path is for instant, 2 color X is for both kind of poisons, green x is for Deadly/instant only.

Red is red because i forgot the trash was also undead.

author: Rheinwg
content:
Tower of Karazhan:
On trash:

- The entire tower is filled with mixed enemies, pick your poison (lol) and stick to it, prio the enemies you can hurt.
- Before Gnarlmoon you face Humanoids, Beast and Undeads. Use instant
- Between Gnarlmoon and Incantagos you can only find Dragons, use instant
- Between Incantagos and Anomalus the packs are Dragons and elementals, pick a posion.
- After Anomalus most of the enemies are undead, elementals or mechanicals, use dissolvent
- After Chess you gonna find Undeads, and right after that pack all of the enemies are either humanoids or demons. Use Diss and the Instant.

Bosses: 
- Anomalus, Rupturan and Chess: Dissolvent and Corrosive 2+1 depending on the spec.
- Medivh: Can be hurt with any kind of poisons, but you should be using Mind numbing if you are combat. Diss for Assa
- Every other boss can only be hurt with Deadly and instant. Combat and Sub uses Deadly 5+4, Assa uses Instant.

Edit: I tested it and it seems like they removed the inmunties on the worgens and the demons, making it a bit less of an issue.

content:
So, just going off by that incantagos (cuz he died on gnarlmoon?)

- He should be using the right poisons (Deadly 5 + Instant on incantagos for example). Same goes for naxx, where he can use Deadly+Corrosive on most fights.
- He should prepare more, the fight lasted for 4m and that should be enough for him to use mark 3 times and shadow 4 times. Is kind of difficuclt to tell if he had the chance to do so, but is some thing he should at least aim for. (the fight really did last 4mins?)
- He used A LOT of eviscerates, and i cant understand why, maybe he tried to keep up TotT? but is always preferable to keep tott up with high cp
- He could have a better SnD uptime, his other sub rogue got almost double the uptime and that is pretty big. (logs sometimes dont regiser snd correctly, keep that in mind)
- Oddly enough neither of them used garrote, which is kinda important, you get a lot of cp for a cheap price.
- Venomous poison is a bad trinket for him, he shouldn't be using that

Incantagos can be a messy fight, sometimes you cannot hit the target, so having non-perfect performance is understandable, but he should be working on improving that. Also, i dont see many buffs on him, but maybe the logs didnt record that so i suppose he was fully buffed with consumes etc.

Also, as a sidenote, why are you guys running 2 sub rogues, and who was doing IEA that run?

Im checking his Naxx, and his patchwerk looks decent. But same thing applies, he should improve his SnD uptime, and use the correct poisons (he did on some bosses tho). 

A HUGE THING for sub rogues is the AQ20 2p set bonus, he should be using that forever pretty much.

Also, something that really helps is to allow him to gather combo points bfore the fight, this goes for any rogue, is awesome to be able to start the fight with 1 combo point already on the enemy, for a lot of reasons.
